core.text: Commit early to the main hypothesis that a fixed 300 rpm, 60-second run can repeatedly achieve the bounded final-sample target without optical stability controlling cessation. The stipulated final attenuations 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207 already meet the target in one trial, contradicting universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm. Reliable repeat success remains unobserved.

Operating construction: perform six fresh, rinsed-vessel trials using 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye, the same bottle, fixed addition location and locked camera. Command 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, then stop until sampling at second 120. Never restart because images fail the preferred rule. Keep the spill tray in use and stop if liquid escapes.

Log five-second side readings, frames, depression and specks as diagnostics. Record commanded speed, cessation and duration. At second 120 withdraw 1 mL from each marked elevation within ten seconds, alternating low-to-high and high-to-low sampling order across trials. Use water and common-aliquot references; report raw attenuations, normalized spread and every failure above 4 percent. Repeated success would support this construction only within the stipulated recipe.

residue.text: Agitation-generated image disturbance and an optical-to-agitation return loop remain mechanism hypotheses. Specks do not identify bubbles; matched 900 rpm final samples and isolated bubble measurements are absent. Convergence on the timer construction does not resolve that mechanism.

Neither relative total stirring-time savings nor relative 900 rpm sample performance is established. Commanded rpm lacks independent verification. Reference repeatability is not calibration, and sampling can disturb gradients; order-dependent success would weaken the main account.

Six trials offer limited replication. Other viscosities, solutes, vessel sizes and continuous operation remain untested; the outcome supports only this synthetic sample proxy, without claims of real chemical or human benefit.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds reliably satisfies the final depth-sample proxy in this recipe, so sustained high-speed optical convergence is dispensable.
tension.account_b: Rival hypothesis: the observed lower-speed success was exceptional or sampling-mediated; fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds generally leaves depth gradients.
tension.prediction_a: Across the prescribed repeats, final-vial spreads remain at most 4 percent without systematic sampling-order dependence, even when side checks exceed 4 percent.
tension.prediction_b: Across the same repeats, final-vial spreads repeatedly exceed 4 percent or success varies systematically with sampling order. Such results undermine reliable sufficiency, but do not prove 900 rpm necessary.
